Subject: Redwood private offer — request on phased discounts and reseller refund

Hi Karthik / Ben,

Thanks for the call this morning — we loved the latency numbers you showed. Before we send PO, procurement has a couple of asks we need baked into the private offer:

1) Graduated discount schedule tied to usage tiers (we want pricing to step down as we hit monthly thresholds).
2) A clear refund/credit flow if our reseller (CloudBridge) needs to return credits to us because of downstream returns — procurement insists that the credit path is documented and auditable.
3) Billing cadence: Can you invoice us directly for the committed tier and pass-through any reseller credits as line-item adjustments?

Can you share an updated term sheet and a short diagram of the refund flow (who issues credits and how they map back to the PO)? Samir is copied on thread and will own the legal/procurement review.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Cloud Platform — AcmeTech

Subject: Re: Redwood private offer — request on phased discounts and reseller refund

Elena — appreciate the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can accommodate a graduated discount schedule and a documented refund/credit flow. Notes below and attaching an updated term sheet draft.

High-level proposal: 
- Graduated discounts are implemented as monthly usage bands (0-5TB, 5-20TB, 20TB+) with stepped unit prices; tiers evaluated at month-end and next invoice reflects the tiered effective price.
- Reseller refunds: when CloudBridge issues a downstream credit, they will provide a signed credit memo referencing your PO number. Redwood will use that memo to issue a corresponding credit against your next invoice. We will also log the credit in the Console audit timeline for traceability.
- Invoicing options: default is Redwood invoices AcmeTech directly for committed capacity and overage; reseller credits show as deduction line items. If you prefer pass-through invoicing via CloudBridge, we can map that, but it requires distributor agreement and alternate invoice routing.

I've attached: Redwood_PrivateOffer_TermSheet_v3.pdf (draft with graduated schedule) and a simple diagram of the reseller refund flow. Ben — can you confirm the operational steps and whether we need a special field on the PO for CloudBridge credit memos? Camila — FYI on billing ops / invoice path.

Next steps suggested: 1) Elena / Samir review term sheet + diagram; 2) Redwood legal prepares the narrow amendment for the PO; 3) DocuSign for signature.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Platform Sales
Redwood Inference

Quick operational notes (adding detail for procurement):

1) Timing of tier evaluation: we run monthly reconciliation on the 2nd business day. If usage in a closed month pushes you into a higher discount band retroactively, we apply a credit on the next invoice. We won’t rebill historical months to new higher prices — credits only.

2) Required fields on credit memos: PO number, reseller name (CloudBridge), affected SKU lines, credit amount, and a short reason code. That is our minimum for automated processing. If CloudBridge supplies anything less, we'll route to manual ops and the credit may be delayed.

3) Auditability: credits will be visible in the Redwood Console under Billing -> Credits, with a link to the vendor memo and an internal audit id. We can provide a weekly CSV export for your finance team during onboarding weeks.

4) Edge-case: if CloudBridge issues a credit > 50% of a given monthly invoice, we require a reconciliation call before applying auto-credits (fraud/returns safeguard).

I'll attach a one-page operational checklist for CloudBridge to follow during onboarding and a sample credit memo template. Happy to walk Samir through it.

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
